counterfactual_missing_items: Multiple viral serologies including CMV, EBV, Coxsackievirus, Echovirus, Parvovirus B19, and Herpes virus 1/2 were negative
Episodes of advanced AV block grade 2 Mobitz type 1 and 2
decisive_items: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin: 128.00 pg/ml initially, peaked at 142.00 pg/ml
Echocardiography: Left ventricle diastolic diameter of 59 mm, hypokinetic left ventricle with EF 50%
Cardiac MRI: Showed slightly increased global T1 and T2 mapping values, minimal hyperintensity of pericardium without effusion
response.rationale: R1 uniquely integrates both pericardial and myocardial involvement: pleuritic chest pain, PR-segment changes, pericardial hyperintensity, elevated troponin, T1/T2 elevation, and LV hypokinesis. R5 captures only pericarditis and misses the myocardial injury. R6 is weakened by negative viral serologies, R7 by normal coronary CTA, R4 by lack of erythema migrans/Lyme serology, R3 by non-syphilitic lesions and remote treated syphilis, and C1 contradicts its own span by claiming effusion when the raw text says without effusion.

rejected.why: Remote treated syphilis and vesicular/umbilicated genital lesions do not explain acute myopericarditis or AV block; no active syphilis serology.
Genital vesicular/umbilicated lesions are not erythema migrans, and there is no tick exposure or Lyme serology; AV block alone is nonspecific.
Negative viral serologies contradict a viral myocarditis label, and it misses the pericardial involvement.
Normal coronary CT angiography and PR-segment rather than ST-segment changes argue against ACS; troponin elevation is explained by myopericarditis.
The raw span says 'without effusion,' so 'with minimal effusion' is unsupported and internally contradictory; also incomplete.
